resources.string: Granule marker position from the basal side
Distance from basal edge to marker
For drawn height H and basal offset d, marker position = 100 × d / H as a percentage of height measured from the basal edge. Apical tip to marker = H − d.

This model follows an open-type enteroendocrine cell in the intestinal lining. Its narrow apical tip contacts the lumen, but secretory granules cluster toward the tissue-facing side, where the cell releases signals. On the drawing, the basal edge is zero and the apical tip is the far end of the same line. A single dot represents the granule region and stays in the basal half. The lengths use arbitrary drawing units (u) and do not measure cell dimensions, granule distributions, or hormone release.
